item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 310522
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico (EP95):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located well offshore of southwestern Mexico remain
disorganized. However, environmental conditions appear conducive for
gradual development, and a tropical depression is expected to form
within the next couple of days while the system continues to move
west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a couple of days. Some gradual development is
possible thereafter while it moves slowly westward across the
central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Karina Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 310842
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026
 
...KARINA INTENSIFIES INTO A CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE AS IT CONTINUES 
WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.2N 124.4W
ABOUT 1020 MI...1640 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...942 MB...27.82 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was 
located near latitude 17.2 North, longitude 124.4 West. Karina is 
moving toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this motion is 
expected to continue through Monday. A turn toward the 
west-northwest is forecast to begin on Tuesday. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 145 mph (230 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional strengthening is 
possible on Monday, followed by fluctuations in intensity through 
the middle part of this week. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 942 mb (27.82 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast 
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next 
couple of days and will likely spread northward to southern 
California on Monday through midweek. These swells are likely to 
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please 
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 310847
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026

Karina has continued to rapidly intensify. Since the previous 
advisory, cold cloud top temperatures below -75 C wrapped back 
around northern side of the hurricane while the eye is making an 
attempt to clear out some. In response, the objective UW-CIMSS ADT 
intensity estimate, after plateauing earlier, has begun to rise 
again, with the latest value at T6.6/129 kt. It is worth noting the 
majority of the other objective estimates are 6-12 h old, likely to 
to the lack of recent microwave imagery. The 06 UTC TAFB subjective 
Dvorak estimate was constrained lower at CI 5.5/102 kt, though the 
Data-T number was also 6.5/125 kt. The initial intensity will be 
set at 125 kt for this advisory, making Karina a formidable Category 
4 hurricane.  

Karina continues to move off generally westward, estimated at 275 
degrees at 8 kt. A narrow but extensive mid-level ridge is parked to 
the north of the hurricane, and this feature will likely remain the 
dominant steering impact on Karina over the next 3-5 days. Towards 
the end of the forecast period, the original ridge becomes eroded by 
a mid-latitude trough digging into the western US coast, but a more 
meridional oriented ridge takes its place to the northwest of 
Karina, which should act to gradually slow its forward motion. Once 
again there has been another leftward shift in the guidance, and the 
latest NHC track forecast has also been adjusted in that direction, 
splitting the difference between the latest HFIP Corrected Consensus 
Approach (HCCA) and Google DeepMind (GDMI) guidance. 

Environmental conditions over Karina remain favorable, and there is 
still some time for the hurricane to intensify a bit more in the 
short-term. However, it also is possible the system will soon start 
to undergo inner-core fluctuations like eyewall replacement cycles 
(ERCs), though there has not been any recent microwave imagery to 
determine if such an event is preparing to take place. Another 
factor to consider is that beyond the next 24-36 h, Karina might 
find itself in environmental conditions favorable for the hurricane 
to develop Annular characteristics, which could slow its rate of 
weakening despite the storm moving over gradually cooling 
sea-surface temperatures. Thus, the NHC intensity forecast is on the 
high side of the guidance envelope for a large portion of the 
forecast period, sticking pretty close to the latest HCCA intensity 
forecast. A somewhat faster rate of weakening is possible by the end 
of the forecast period when Karina is forecast to cross the 26 C 
sea-surface temperature isotherm. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
